summary: Every prompt the OS builds is sized on purpose: the confirmation question gets its own ~12K budget with a labelled truncation and a PR reference, every OS call records how big its input was, a measured backstop refuses an absurd one out loud, workers pass references instead of payloads, and a measurement proves trimmed evidence still judges the same.

children.title: Size the assumption-confirmation question for what it is, not for the panel
children.spec_section: 2 — The confirmation question gets its own budget, sized for what it is
children.description: Own src/jarvis/autoreview.py, Daemon._confirmation_evidence in daemon.py with its one production caller, and the new catalog field. Do NOT edit src/jarvis/evidence.py (a test walks its AST, imports inside functions included) and do NOT touch diff_chars=150000 or anything the validation panel reads. Tests: tests/test_autoreview_confirm.py (its stub_evidence helper returns the old 2-tuple; tests/test_autoreview.py:1508 is the second caller) and tests/test_catalog.py. Siblings own the transport's measurement and its ceiling — measure and cap nothing at the transport here.
children.acceptance: A confirmation question over a huge diff is shorter than the panel's 150000-char budget AND carries a truncation marker naming a dropped file that appears in the stat; both asserted in one test. Every confirmation question carries the PR link and head SHA, truncated or not, and never prints a branch name as a SHA. Full stat and full file list survive a budget that keeps no diff at all. decide_evidence scans the text actually stored.

children.title: Every OS-side model call records how big its own prompt was
children.spec_section: 3 — The transport measures its own input, and the OS can see it
children.description: Own claude_cli.run_headless_result and HeadlessResult, agent_usage.record, the two additive agent_calls columns with their ADDED_COLUMNS migration, and the jarvis cost / jarvis inspect renderers (locate them with find_referencing_symbols on CentralStore.agent_calls). Cap NOTHING: the transport backstop, neo_store.ask's ceiling and the digest clip are a sibling's, and it needs your columns to read its default off a real seat prompt. Tests: tests/test_agent_usage.py, tests/test_schema_upgrade.py, tests/test_cost_report.py, tests/test_inspection.py. Leave autoreview.py alone.
children.acceptance: Stored sizes equal len(prompt) and len(system_prompt) exactly for a call with two distinct known sizes. The two columns reach a database that already has agent_calls and old rows read as 0. A call that raised ClaudeCliError records nothing at all, pinned by a test. jarvis cost names the largest OS-side inputs by kind and jarvis inspect names the biggest one for the order.

children.title: A backstop ceiling that refuses an absurd OS prompt out loud, never silently
children.spec_section: 4 — The backstop ceiling: refuse an absurd prompt out loud, never silently
children.description: Own the new catalog ceiling, the refusal in claude_cli.run_headless_result, the hard ceiling in neo_store.ask, the input clip in digest.summarise, and the inbox row plus attention flag at each consumer's call site. The prompt-size columns already exist — read your default off a real maximal seat prompt with them and comment the number. Tests: tests/test_transport_resilience.py (mirror its crash-is-not-a-verdict set), tests/test_autoreview_confirm.py, tests/test_validation_seats.py, tests/test_digest.py, tests/test_catalog.py. Do not touch autoreview.py or add an ALARM_KINDS entry.
children.acceptance: A full-sized validation round with a 150000-char diff still reaches a verdict and writes every seat's agent_calls row — the ceiling refuses none. An over-ceiling call raises a ClaudeCliError subclass before any subprocess runs, and the Neo question stays claimable, the seat writes no opinion, the assumption stays pending with no confirm_question_id, and no agent_calls row claims success. The refusal writes one inbox row and one attention flag naming kind, size and work order. neo_store.ask refuses an oversized question with the reason on the record. A long question is clipped before it is digested.

children.title: A worker passes a reference, and is refused before it pastes a payload
children.spec_section: 5 — The worker side: pass a reference, and be refused when you paste a payload
children.description: Own src/jarvis/hooks.py (the new check inside preflight_decision), concision.py, worker_brief.py and the dispatch env var. Nothing that reaches an OS-built model prompt is yours: the transport, neo_store and autoreview belong to siblings. Tests: tests/test_concision_mechanisms.py (mirror the finish-summary set), tests/test_concision.py, tests/test_worker_brief.py. Drive the whole preflight_decision entry point, never the new check alone, or a later move past the jarvis auto-allow goes unnoticed. Do not raise CORE_BUDGET_CHARS=3800; fit the rule by cutting.
children.acceptance: `jarvis neo ask proj "$(git diff)"` is denied through the real hook entry point with a message naming what to pass instead (PR URL, commit SHA, path plus line range). An oversized wo send body is denied. concision.py still imports only the standard library, pinned by a test. The hook cap and sections.QUESTION_MAX_CHARS are reconciled in a comment.

children.title: Measure that a trimmed confirmation packet judges the same as the full diff
children.spec_section: 6 — Proof: does a trimmed packet judge the same?
children.description: Call the shipped trimming path and read the arms' sizes off the recorded prompt-size columns; invent neither. The deliverable is a measurement: touch nothing under src/jarvis/. Files: evals/llm/test_confirm_evidence_ab.py, copying the JARVIS_EVALS_LLM gating and the one-substring-cut arm discipline of evals/llm/test_house_style_ab.py and carrying pytest.mark.scenario, plus tests/test_confirm_evidence_ab_harness.py modelled on tests/test_stakes_classifier_ab_harness.py. Only the agreement number needs a real model; arm construction and scoring must be provable with fake_claude.
children.acceptance: The unsafe direction is scored separately and asserted zero: no case where the trimmed arm approves what the full arm denied or escalated. The harness test proves a hand-built deny/approve pair fails the run. Safe-direction disagreement is reported as a number, not a failure. Both arms' input sizes are reported from the recorded prompt-size columns.
